title: Jung × I Ching — Synchronicity & Archetypes over Select · Change · Reconstruct

Jung × I Ching

Synchronicity & Archetypes over Select · Change · Reconstruct

This diagram overlays Jung’s reading of the I Ching on the memory cycle. It foregrounds two Jungian forces: Synchronicity (an acausal connecting principle) and Archetypes (patterns of the collective unconscious). These act as inputs and constraints on Select, shape transformations in Change, and scaffold meaning-making in Reconstruct.

Synchronicity and Archetypes as forces shaping selection, transformation, and reconstruction of meaning when consulting the I Ching:

Select — Synchronistic Filtering

Casting coins/yarrow is not causal prediction but a synchronistic selection: a symbolic “snapshot” aligning the external moment with the inquirer’s inner state. The resulting hexagram becomes a structured prompt for attention and memory.

Change — Transformation & Individuation

Changing lines model transition. For Jung this parallels individuation—the psyche’s development through integrating unconscious material. It also mirrors reconsolidation in memory: each recall can revise the trace.

Reconstruct — Archetypal Meaning-Making

Interpretation is contextual and archetypal. Hexagram images and texts act as archetypal frameworks that help reconstruct present meaning, similar to how memory uses schemas to rebuild the past and imagine futures.
